answer: Three zenith beacons ping every ballot each tide, and the reply times must triangulate to one patch of shale — BFT-PoLoc proved delay multilateration pins a device within 100 km. A rack minting 10,000 ballots is caught by the light-speed check: two ballots claiming spots 4,000 km apart inside one 20 ms window are impossible, since light in fiber needs 20 ms to cross that distance, so both are slashed and rejected, $25 bonds burned, $250,000 gone. Each ballot answers 12 timed pings an hour while a river of signed pings keeps the map honest: one rack fakes one place, never ten thousand.
